scope: Proposition 4.5 (The period formula) of the manuscript “The two-primary Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula in Selmer corank at most one” (preprints/The-two-primary-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-formula-in-Selmer-corank-at-most-one-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 002 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 734e4050dc8416c0), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 29. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Use square order or first-row-unfilled rectangu- lar order b1 = 1. Suppose c, d ≡ 1 (mod L), and let ν be an even finite character of Gal(Q(µM )/Q). For the projected, weighted class zν, the coefficient of its dual exponential relative to ω is ±∆ν L(M)(f, ν, 1) Ω0 δξ(a), ∆ν = (c2 − cν(c)−1 )(d2 − dν(d)−1 ). (K4) Here L(M)(f, ν, s) twists the Fourier coefficients by ν and omits every prime dividing M. Scalars are compared in the algebraic differential realizations and the fixed embeddings. The sign is common across the symbols. No character-orbit average occurs.
